title: Unified Inference: Product Overview, PRD, Roadmap & Pricing — Q1 2028 Release
author: Asha Patel
summary: Comprehensive product document for Unified Inference covering the product overview, PRD (requirements and design), 2028 roadmap and themes, pricing & packaging guidance, and release notes for the Q1 2028 launch.
body:
Purpose
This document consolidates the product overview, prioritized requirements (PRD), high-level design specs, roadmap and thematic priorities for 2028, recommended pricing & packaging, and the Q1 2028 release notes for Unified Inference. It is intended for engineering, product, sales, and go-to-market teams to align on scope, delivery plan, and customer-facing messaging.

1) Product overview
- One-line: Unified Inference provides a single API and operational surface for running high-performance LLM inference across Hosted API, Dedicated capacity, and Private deployments.
- Key value props:
  - Predictable latency and cost across deployments (hosted, reserved, private).
  - Unified developer experience (same API, SDKs, rollout primitives).
  - Cost-aware controls: batching, prefix/KV caching, quantization profiles, and model routing policies.
- Primary personas:
  - ML Engineers integrating models into product features.
  - Platform engineers standardizing inference across teams.
  - CTO/Infrastructure leads evaluating cost/SLAs for production LLMs.

2) Goals & success metrics (OKRs)
- Goal 1: Increase adoption of Dedicated by mid-market customers. Key metrics: 50 new Dedicated contracts by EOY 2028; average committed throughput per customer >= 10k RPS-equivalent tokens.
- Goal 2: Reduce per-token unit cost for common text-generation workloads by 20% vs. baseline. Metrics: 20% lower cost-per-1k-tokens for top-5 workload clusters (measured QPS-weighted).
- Goal 3: Maintain production reliability: Platform availability >= 99.95% for hosted API; Dedicated deployments SLA target 99.9%. Latency SLOs: p50 <= 60ms token, p95 <= 350ms token for typical 1k-seq workloads on dedicated hardware.

3) Scope & out-of-scope for Q1 2028 release
- In-scope:
  - Launch of unified model routing policy editor (UI + API).
  - Redwood Optimize vNext: automated quantization & batching recommendations integrated into Console.
  - Pricing & packaging update introducing a new Mid-market Dedicated tier and clearer packaging for Private on-prem licensing.
  - Release notes and migration guide for customers on legacy Dedicated plans.
- Out-of-scope:
  - New model training/finetuning capabilities.
  - Full multi-tenant on-prem control plane (targeted for Q3 2028).

4) Product requirements (high-level, prioritized)
- MUST: Unified API parity across Hosted/Dedicated/Private for generation, chat, embeddings, and tool-calling.
- MUST: Model routing policies supporting rules by region, latency, cost, and model family; automatic fallback to compatible variants.
- MUST: Console support for Redwood Optimize recommendations: quantization profile suggestions, batch window tuning, and cache TTLs.
- SHOULD: Billing preview in Console for recommended optimize actions (est. cost delta).
- SHOULD: Migration path for existing Dedicated customers (config translation tool + rollback policy).
- COULD: Simple self-serve private deployment for single-region customers with KMS integration.

5) Design specs (high level)
- Architecture overview:
  - Control plane: unified policy service, model catalog, billing adapter, and recommendation engine. Owned by eng-platform.
  - Data plane: runtime instances (hosted fleet, dedicated pools, private agents) expose the same inference API surface. Runtime selects kernels and quantization profiles at request time.
  - Console: React-based UI with policy editor, cost previews, and rollout dashboards.
  - Observability: token-level traces, per-route latency/cost histograms, and quality regressions dashboard (linked to evals).

- Important design decisions and rationale:
  1. Policy evaluation in control plane (vs local): centralizes telemetry and simplifies rollout tracing; fallback executed locally to minimize latency on failure.
  2. Recommendation engine outputs "actions" (quantize model XYZ -> q4_0) rather than automatically mutating serving configs. Product decision: recommend by default, allow auto-apply via an enterprise opt-in.
  3. Billing estimates use a conservative cost model (5% overhead) to avoid underestimating bill impact for customers.

- Data & schema requirements (table form):
  | Field | Type | Description | Required? | Example |
  | model_id | string | canonical model id in catalog | yes | redwood/gptx-7b |
  | quant_profile | string | recommended quantization profile | conditional | q4_0 |
  | expected_savings_pct | string | estimator for token cost reduction | conditional | 18% |
  | rollout_policy | string | canary/blue-green/manual | yes | canary |

(above rendered as ASCII table for Confluence)

6) Roadmap & themes (2028, high level)
- Theme A — "Operational economics": focus on lowering deployed unit cost (recommendations, caching, smarter batching). Q1 deliverables: Optimize vNext integration + billing preview. Q2: Automated quantization rollout for Dedicated.
- Theme B — "Enterprise readiness": Private deployment UX, audit logging, and improved support SLAs. Q1 deliverable: Private pricing & packaging; Q3: on-prem installer v1.
- Theme C — "Latency-first runtime": kernel selection and small-sequence optimizations. Q1 deliverable: p95 improvements for 128-512 seq lengths on Dedicated.
- Milestones (quarterly):
  - Q1 2028: Policy editor, Optimize vNext, Pricing & packaging update, published migration guides.
  - Q2 2028: Auto-apply quantization (enterprise opt-in), Dedicated autoscaling policy improvements.
  - Q3 2028: Private on-prem GA (single-region), expanded KMS integrations.

7) Pricing & packaging notes (guidance for GTM and sales)
- Pricing principles:
  - Transparent, usage-based for Hosted (per-token generation & per-embedding unit).
  - Committed monthly/annual pricing for Dedicated (reservations + overage rates).
  - Private: platform license + support tier + optional managed upgrades.
- Suggested packaging (three tiers):
  - Hosted (Self-serve): pay-as-you-go; recommended list price "$0.12 per 1k generation tokens" (baseline model family), "$0.06 per 1k embedding tokens". Free tier 100k tokens/mo for new signups.
  - Dedicated (Mid-market): monthly commitment bands:
    - Bronze: $5k/mo commit -> baseline throughput 200 RPS-equivalent, 10% discount vs hosted.
    - Silver: $20k/mo commit -> baseline throughput 1k RPS-equivalent, 25% discount.
    - Gold: $75k/mo commit -> baseline throughput 4k RPS-equivalent, 40% discount + faster support SLA.
  - Private (Enterprise): negotiated license fee + support (typical range $150k–$1M/yr depending on scope) + optional managed services.
- Billing & metering notes:
  - Metering is token-based with model-family multipliers for expensive decoders (e.g., gptx-70b * 3.2).
  - Price preview UI included in Console for Optimize recommendations (estimates only).

8) Release notes — Q1 2028 (what shipped)
- New features:
  - Unified Model Routing Policy Editor (Console + API): define rules by latency, cost, and region; supports canary rollout and automatic fallback.
  - Redwood Optimize vNext integrated recommendations in Console (quantization suggestions, batching window, cache TTL).
  - New Dedicated Mid-market packaging and migration guide.
  - Billing preview for Optimize recommendations (UI only).
- Improvements:
  - p95 latency improved by ~18% for 128–512 seqs on Dedicated pool types via kernel selection updates.
  - Observability: added per-route token-cost breakdown and token-level tracing hooks for faster triage.
- Bug fixes:
  - Fixed a rare session state leak affecting long-running chat sessions (>2 hours).
  - Resolved race in policy-evaluation for multi-region failover.

9) Rollout & migration plan (step-by-step)
1. Internal staged rollout: feature flags toggled for internal teams (eng, se, selected customers) for 2 weeks.
2. Beta program: invite 25 early adopters (mix of startups + mid-market) for a 6-week beta; collect telemetry and customer feedback.
3. Documentation: publish migration guide, CLI config translator, and automated tests for migration scenarios.
4. General availability: open sign-ups and sales enablement with pricing sheet and playbook.
5. Post-GA: 30-day rollback policy for Dedicated customers (control-plane rollback + config restore script).

10) Ownership & support 
- Product owner: Asha Patel (product).
- Eng leads: 
  - Control plane & Console: Priya Singh (eng-platform).
  - Runtime & kernel selection: Evan Li (eng-serving-runtime).
  - Observability & SLOs: Diego Martinez (eng-sre).
- Support path: Tier 1 -> success -> eng-oncall; escalation playbook referenced: /confluence/customer-success-and-support/escalation-playbook.
- SLOs and operational thresholds (for product docs):
  - Hosted API availability: 99.95% monthly.
  - Dedicated SLA (Gold): 99.9% monthly availability.
  - Latency targets: p50 <= 60ms token, p95 <= 350ms token (typical 1k sequence on dedicated hardware).
  - Error budget policy: 14-day burn window; automated rollback if error budget exceed 75% within 72 hours for critical routes.

11) Risks & mitigations
- Risk: Automated quantization may regress quality for edge-case prompts. Mitigation: require manual review for production-critical routes; A/B evaluations against golden prompt sets before auto-apply.
- Risk: Pricing confusion for customers when recommended actions reduce cost but change model behavior. Mitigation: billing preview + explicit customer approval flows.
- Risk: Private deployment complexity and long sales cycles. Mitigation: publish a clear reference architecture and pre-validated on-prem installer for target platforms.

12) Appendix & links
- Migration tools: CLI translator example: 
  - sh migrate-config.sh --source legacy-dedicated.json --target unified-policy.json
- Telemetry & evals: link to eval-harness and prompt-sets-and-benchmarks in team wiki.
- Contact: product@redwood.ai, eng-platform@redwood.ai.

Document maintenance: Product owner to update this page for each minor release. Major roadmap changes require product review and infra/finance signoff.
